prompts: Mike finds the drawing Will made of the party — the one where the wizard looks a little too much like Mike. It's tucked in a book Will lent him. Neither of them mentions it, but the air changes.
Snowball dance, alternate ending. Will doesn't run to the bathroom this time. He asks Mike to dance, and to his own shock, the words actually come out.
It's the summer after Vecna. Will and Mike are the only two awake at 3 a.m. in the Byers' new house in California, sitting on the floor because neither can sleep.
Mike drives to Lenora to visit for spring break. Will meant to act normal. He does not act normal.
A thunderstorm knocks the power out during a campaign. Everyone else goes home. Will and Mike are left with a single candle and a conversation they've been avoiding for years.
Will overhears Mike on the phone with El, saying the words 'I don't think it was ever really about her.' He shouldn't have heard that. He can't un-hear it.
The painting. Will finally tells Mike the truth about who really commissioned it. Set it right after the van scene in season 4 — or wherever you want.
Post-canon: they're moving into a tiny apartment together 'as roommates.' There is one bed. There has always, somehow, been one bed.
Mike keeps the walkie-talkie under his pillow long after they should've outgrown it. One night, static — then Will's voice, calling him like it's 1983 again.
Will teaches Mike how to paint. Mike is terrible at it. Neither of them cares, because Will keeps having to lean in to fix Mike's grip on the brush.
Truth or dare with the party, but Max is merciless and she has known about both of them for years.
It's Will's birthday and Mike shows up with a gift that says, without saying, everything he's never had the courage to.
They fight. A real one, years in the making. Say something you can't take back — then figure out how they find their way back to each other.
The Upside Down took something from Will that only Mike ever noticed was missing. Post-recovery, Mike is determined to help him find it again.
College. Will and Mike end up at the same school by a coincidence that is absolutely not a coincidence, and share a dorm hallway.
A rainy road trip. One motel. Mike falls asleep on Will's shoulder in the car and Will doesn't dare move for two hundred miles.
El and Will have a quiet conversation about Mike. It goes gentler, and braver, than either of them expected.
Mike memorized the sound of Will's laugh sometime around 1984 and only just realized it. He's realizing a lot of things lately.
The party graduates high school. Everyone's talking about the future. Will can only think about one specific part of his.
Will draws Mike, in secret, for the hundredth time. This time Mike walks in before he can hide the sketchbook.
A slow dance in an empty gym while cleaning up after a school event nobody else stayed for.
Mike writes a letter he never intends to send. Will finds it. Take it from there.
Christmas at the Wheelers'. Mistletoe is involved, and Nancy is enjoying this far too much.
They're both grown now — late twenties — and reunite at a party reunion after years apart. Everything they never said is still sitting right there between them.
The Void. Will is pulled somewhere dark again, and the only anchor pulling him back is a voice he'd know anywhere.
Mike gets jealous of someone new in Will's life in California, and it forces him to admit — at least to himself — exactly what that jealousy means.
D&D made flesh: Will is the cleric, Mike is the paladin sworn to the party. When the healing runs out mid-quest, Mike is the one kneeling in the dirt refusing to let him go.
Will is a sorcerer who never asked for his magic, and Mike is the knight assigned to guard him from the people who want it. Neither of them is very good at keeping their distance.
A witch and his familiar. Will's spells have gone strange lately, and every single one of them keeps pointing at the boy who was supposed to just be a black cat on his windowsill.
Hogwarts AU. Mike is the Gryffindor who shouldn't be in the Hufflepuff common room at midnight, and Will is the one who keeps leaving the door unlocked anyway.
Mike is a pirate captain with a bad reputation and worse manners. Will is the thing tangled in his nets that is very much not a fish, and very much not letting go of his wrist.
Vampire AU. Will has been nineteen since 1986 and Mike has just recognized him across a crowded bar, forty years too late and not aged a day in his memory.
Ghost story: Mike buys a crumbling house in Hawkins and the boy who's been haunting it since the eighties knows things about him he never told anyone alive.
Angel and demon, both stationed in the same nothing town, both bad at their jobs, both filing reports that leave out the important parts about each other.
Rockstar Mike is playing the biggest show of his life and the tattoo artist he keeps flying across three states to see is standing in the wings again.
Two teachers, one staff room. Mike teaches English, Will teaches art, and the kids figured it out approximately a year before either of them did.
Will is a figure skater and Mike plays hockey and they share the same terrible 5 a.m. ice time. It starts as a turf war.
Summer job AU: Mike is stuck in the Scoops Ahoy sailor hat and Will is delivering for Surfer Boy Pizza. Both of them keep inventing reasons to be at the other's counter.
The Hawkins arcade, closing shift, 1985. Mike has one quarter left and Will is the only person who's ever beaten his high score.
Coffee shop, present day. Will has written the same wrong name on the cup for a month and Mike has stopped correcting him.
Regency AU: a painter of no particular fortune and the heir who keeps commissioning portraits he does not need.
Ancient Greece — a soldier and the oracle who keeps seeing the same ending and refuses to say it out loud.
1800s expedition, somewhere cold and unmapped. Two men, one tent, and a journal that stops being about the survey around week six.
Soulmate AU where the mark shows up the first time the other person says your name like it matters. Will's arrived when he was eight. Mike's took a lot longer.
Goth Will and punk Mike, sharing a cigarette neither of them wants behind a venue in 1989.
Single-parent AU: Will is raising a kid alone and Mike is the neighbor who keeps showing up with groceries nobody asked for and doesn't leave.
Beauty and the Beast, roughly: a monster in a locked house who is desperate to be seen as a person, and the boy who keeps coming back to the library anyway.
Superhero AU. Mike's powers are loud and public; Will's are quiet and dangerous. The city has picked a favorite and it's the wrong one.
Both of them are nineteen and broke, driving a car that shouldn't make it out of Indiana, with no plan past the next state line.
Zombie apocalypse. Will has been bitten, or thinks he has, and won't let Mike near him. Mike, being Mike, does not respect this at all.
Werewolf AU: the full moon has never scared Will. What scares him is who keeps waiting up in the woods for him to come back.
Modern-day, no monsters, no powers: they're just two boys at the same high school, and the hardest thing in the world is a hand held under a lunch table.

universes.label: Hawkins, as it happened
universes.text: This is the world of the show: Hawkins, the party, and the thing under the town that nobody outside it believes in.

universes.label: No monsters
universes.text: Same town, same people, no Upside Down — nothing has ever come for either of them, so the only thing left to be afraid of is each other.

universes.label: The campaign, for real
universes.text: The campaign is the world: Will is a cleric, Mike is a paladin sworn to the party, and the dice were always going to land here.

universes.label: School of magic
universes.text: They are students at a school of magic, in a castle that keeps rearranging itself around the two of them.

universes.label: The high seas
universes.text: Mike captains a ship with a bad reputation, and the sea gave him Will — who is not entirely a man, and not letting go of his wrist.

universes.label: The long night
universes.text: One of them stopped aging decades ago. Immortality is mostly waiting, and he has been waiting for this face to come back around.

universes.label: A haunting
universes.text: One of them is dead and has not left, and the other has just moved into the house he never stopped living in.

universes.label: Stage lights and ink
universes.text: Mike's band is bigger than anyone planned and Will tattoos out of a shop three states away, which has never once stopped either of them from getting on a plane.

universes.label: Two teachers
universes.text: They teach at the same high school — English and art, adjoining hallways — and their students worked it out roughly a year before they did.

universes.label: Shared ice
universes.text: Will skates figures and Mike plays hockey and the rink gave them the same terrible five in the morning. It started as a turf war.

universes.label: After the end
universes.text: The world ended some months ago. What is left is a road, a rifle between them, and the fact that neither will go on without the other.

timePeriods.label: 1980s canon
timePeriods.text: Set this in the middle of their Hawkins years, when the party still meets in the basement and nobody has left yet.

timePeriods.label: Post-Vecna
timePeriods.text: Set this in the uneasy months after the fight with Vecna, when everyone is pretending to be fine.

timePeriods.label: The California year
timePeriods.text: Set this during the year Will is in Lenora and Mike is in Hawkins, with letters and phone calls doing all the work.

timePeriods.label: Senior year
timePeriods.text: Set this in their last year of high school, with graduation close enough to make every plan feel permanent.

timePeriods.label: Early 1990s
timePeriods.text: Set this in the first years after high school, when they are technically grown and nothing feels settled yet.

timePeriods.label: Adult post-canon
timePeriods.text: Mike and Will are adults now, carrying years of unfinished history with them.

timePeriods.label: College AU
timePeriods.text: Set this at college, where nobody knows who they used to be to each other.

timePeriods.label: Modern AU
timePeriods.text: Set this now, with no Upside Down and no monsters — just the two of them and everything they have never said.

timePeriods.label: An age of quests
timePeriods.text: Set this in an age of long roads, bad kings and worse gods, where a party of six is the only thing standing between a village and the dark.

timePeriods.label: Their school years, elsewhere
timePeriods.text: Set this while they are still students — the same age they were in the basement, in a life that never included Hawkins.

timePeriods.label: The age of sail
timePeriods.text: Set this on open water in a century of charts and superstition, where the map runs out a week west of here.

timePeriods.label: An endless night
timePeriods.text: Set this in a present that never quite gets to morning, where one of them has had far too much time to think about it.

timePeriods.label: The first year after
timePeriods.text: Set this in the first year after everything fell over, close enough to remember what bread tasted like.

relationshipContexts.label: Best friends, unspoken
relationshipContexts.text: They are still best friends in every way that anyone can see, and neither has looked too closely at the rest of it.

relationshipContexts.label: One of them knows
relationshipContexts.text: Will has known what this is for a long time; Mike has not let himself finish the thought.

relationshipContexts.label: Mutual but unspoken
relationshipContexts.text: Both of them know their friendship stopped being simple, but neither has said it out loud.

relationshipContexts.label: Recently confessed
relationshipContexts.text: One of them said it out loud recently, and they are both still learning what the days after that look like.

relationshipContexts.label: Secretly dating
relationshipContexts.text: They have been together for a while now, and nobody else knows.

relationshipContexts.label: Established
relationshipContexts.text: They are together, past the terrified part, and the people who matter know.

relationshipContexts.label: Estranged and reunited
relationshipContexts.text: They have not been close in years, and every old feeling comes back faster than either expected.

relationshipContexts.label: The one that almost was
relationshipContexts.text: Something nearly happened between them once, and they have both spent a long time calling it nothing.

tones.label: Tender
tones.text: Keep the scene tender and unhurried; let the smallest gestures carry the weight.

tones.label: Awkward
tones.text: Let the scene be awkward — half-finished sentences, badly timed honesty, nobody smooth.

tones.label: Nostalgic
tones.text: Keep the scene nostalgic and intimate, aware of how much history is in the room with them.

tones.label: Angsty
tones.text: Let it hurt. Neither of them gets to say the easy version of what they mean.

tones.label: Playful
tones.text: Keep it light and teasing, with the real thing sitting just underneath the joke.

tones.label: Suspenseful
tones.text: Hold the tension taut; something is about to go wrong and both of them can feel it.

tones.label: Bittersweet
tones.text: Keep it bittersweet — whatever they get here, they do not get to keep all of it.

tones.label: Chaotic
tones.text: Let it be loud and messy, with the important thing said at exactly the wrong moment.

tones.label: Quiet and domestic
tones.text: Keep it small and domestic; the drama is entirely in what goes unsaid over an ordinary task.

tones.label: Hopeful
tones.text: Let the scene end more open than it began, even if nothing is resolved.

locations.label: Wheeler basement
locations.text: Mike and Will are alone in the Wheeler basement after everyone else leaves an unfinished campaign behind.

locations.label: Castle Byers in the rain
locations.text: They end up in Castle Byers with the rain coming through the roof, too close together because there is nowhere else to sit.

locations.label: The Byers kitchen at 3 a.m.
locations.text: It is three in the morning in the Byers kitchen and neither of them can sleep.

locations.label: Mike's bedroom
locations.text: They are shut in Mike's bedroom during a sleepover, talking in the dark about nothing in particular.

locations.label: The empty school gym
locations.text: The dance is over and they are the only two left in the gym while somebody stacks chairs down the hall.

locations.label: The back of a record store
locations.text: They are hiding out in the back of a record store, going through the same crate for the third time.

locations.label: A stalled car
locations.text: The car has died on a road with no houses on it, and the walk back would take hours.

locations.label: A motel room
locations.text: A trip has stranded them in a motel room with one working lamp and far too much quiet.

locations.label: A dorm hallway
locations.text: It is two in the morning in a dorm hallway, and neither of them is going back inside yet.

locations.label: A tiny shared apartment
locations.text: They are in the small apartment they share, in the middle of an evening that started out ordinary.

locations.label: A reunion porch
locations.text: They find themselves alone on a back porch during a reunion, years after they last really talked.

locations.label: A hospital waiting room
locations.text: They are the only two left in a hospital waiting room, running out of things to say and refusing to leave.

locations.label: Outside a graduation party
locations.text: The graduation party is loud behind them; they have both drifted out to the same dark patch of yard.

locations.label: The van on a long drive
locations.text: Everyone else is asleep in the back of the van and the two of them are awake in the front for hours.

locations.label: A cabin in a storm
locations.text: The storm has them shut inside a borrowed cabin with one blanket and no way to leave.

locations.label: A wrong version of somewhere familiar
locations.text: They are standing in a place they know by heart, except everything in it is subtly, horribly wrong.

locations.label: The arcade at closing
locations.text: The arcade is closing around them and neither has made a move toward the door.

locations.label: Opposite ends of a phone line
locations.text: They are on opposite ends of a phone call that has already run far past the point either can afford.

locations.label: Packing up a house
locations.text: They are packing a house into boxes, and every third thing either of them picks up is a memory neither wants to explain.

locations.label: A late-night diner booth
locations.text: They are in the back booth of a diner that is about to close, splitting the last of the coffee.

locations.label: Camp in a ruined temple
locations.text: The party sleeps in a ruined temple and the two of them take the same watch, again, the way they always somehow do.

locations.label: After the healing spell
locations.text: The fight is over, Will's hands are still shaking from what he had to pour into Mike, and nobody else has come back yet.

locations.label: The top of the tower
locations.text: The highest window in the castle, well after curfew, with the whole grounds asleep underneath them.

locations.label: Detention, together
locations.text: They are being punished for the same thing in the same empty classroom, and there are two hours left of it.

locations.label: The crow's nest
locations.text: Up in the rigging with the crew asleep below, the only two awake on the whole ship.

locations.label: A cove nobody charted
locations.text: A cove that is on no map, warm water, and the understanding that one of them cannot follow the other home.

locations.label: The bar that never closes
locations.text: A bar at the hour when everyone sober has gone, where one of them has been sitting in the same seat for rather more years than he looks.

locations.label: A rooftop, before dawn
locations.text: A rooftop with maybe forty minutes of dark left in it, which is the whole problem.

locations.label: The house that remembers him
locations.text: The front room of a house that has been empty for forty years and is very obviously not empty now.

locations.label: Boxes in the attic
locations.text: An attic full of somebody's whole unfinished life, being sorted by the one person who can see him standing there watching.

locations.label: The dressing room, after
locations.text: Twenty minutes after the encore, ears still ringing, the only person he actually wanted out there sitting on the counter.

locations.label: The chair at closing
locations.text: The shop is shut, the needle is off, and one of them has an hour of being held perfectly still to get through.

locations.label: The staff room at six
locations.text: The staff room long after the buses have gone, two piles of marking and one working coffee machine.

locations.label: The art room after the bell
locations.text: The art room with the chairs still down, paint drying, and someone from the English department who has run out of reasons to be in here.

locations.label: Five in the morning, shared ice
locations.text: An empty rink at five in the morning, one half of it marked out for figures and the other for a net nobody has moved yet.

locations.label: The locker room, taping up
locations.text: An empty locker room, one of them taping the other's wrist because there is nobody else left in the building to do it.

locations.label: A gas station, barricaded
locations.text: A gas station with the doors wedged shut, one night to get through, and something outside that has not gone away.

locations.label: A quiet mile of road
locations.text: A mile of empty highway with nothing on it, which is the closest thing to safe either of them has had in months.

locations.label: Under the lunch table
locations.text: A crowded cafeteria, a table they have sat at for four years, and a hand that nobody above the table can see.

variants.low: Mike notices Will has been sketching him and tries not to make a thing out of it.
variants.medium: Mike finds a drawing Will never meant him to see, and Will knows immediately what he is holding.
variants.high: Mike finds a whole sketchbook of himself, including the pages that make Will's feelings impossible to explain away.

variants.low: A casual conversation about next year reveals they have been imagining very different lives.
variants.medium: Mike learns Will is considering leaving without telling him.
variants.high: Will has already accepted something far away, and Mike finds out that everyone else knew first.

tensions.label: Someone else is in the picture

variants.low: Someone flirts with one of them and the other is unpleasantly surprised by how much he hates it.
variants.medium: One of them has started seeing someone, and the other keeps being aggressively supportive about it.
variants.high: One of them brings a date, and the whole night becomes an exercise in pretending that is fine.

variants.low: An old argument surfaces sideways in a joke that lands wrong.
variants.medium: They restart the fight they never finished, and it is immediately about something else.
variants.high: Everything they have swallowed for years comes out at once, in the worst possible order.

variants.low: A stranger assumes they are together and neither corrects it fast enough.
variants.medium: Someone they know assumes it, out loud, in front of people, and the silence goes on too long.
variants.high: The assumption gets back to someone whose opinion matters, and now it has to be answered.

tensions.label: One of them nearly says it

variants.low: One of them starts a sentence he cannot finish and pretends he was going to say something else.
variants.medium: One of them says something that cannot be passed off as a joke, and does not take it back.
variants.high: One of them says it outright, and the other does not answer for a very long moment.

variants.low: Whatever they were avoiding, they now have to sit in the same small space with it for a while.
variants.medium: They are stuck here for the night, and there is no version of this where they do not talk.
variants.high: They are stuck, one of them is hurt or shaking, and neither can pretend the other does not matter this much.

variants.low: One of them remembers a promise the other assumed was forgotten.
variants.medium: A promise they made as kids turns out to have meant very different things to each of them.
variants.high: One of them realizes the other has been keeping that promise this entire time, at real cost.

variants.low: One of them wakes the other from a nightmare neither wants to describe.
variants.medium: The old feeling is back — the cold on the neck — and only one of them will admit he felt it.
variants.high: It is happening again, it is happening to one of them specifically, and the other cannot fix it.

tensions.label: One of them is hurt and hiding it

variants.low: One of them is clearly not okay and is doing a bad job of hiding it.
variants.medium: One of them is hurt and has been hiding it for days; the other finds out by accident.
variants.high: The hiding stops working in the worst way, and the other has to take care of him with nothing but his hands and whatever is in the room.

variants.low: Something almost happens and then somebody walks in with a question about dinner.
variants.medium: They are interrupted at exactly the wrong second, and neither can find the way back to it.
variants.high: They are interrupted by someone who saw enough, and now there is a second problem.

tensions.label: A letter that was never sent

variants.low: One of them finds a letter that was started and abandoned.
variants.medium: One of them finds a letter the other wrote and never sent, and reads far enough to regret starting.
variants.high: The unsent letter says all of it, and the person it was addressed to is holding it while its author watches.

variants.low: A friend says something offhand that suggests this has been obvious to everyone for years.
variants.medium: It turns out the party has been quietly waiting for them to catch up.
variants.high: One of them learns everyone knew, told the other, and left him to figure it out alone.

tensions.label: One of them goes too far protecting the other

variants.low: One of them steps in on the other's behalf, and it is not entirely welcome.
variants.medium: One of them makes a decision for the other, for his own good, and is caught at it.
variants.high: One of them does something dangerous to keep the other safe and refuses to apologize for it.

tensions.label: They are not who they were

variants.low: One of them has changed in some small way the other keeps noticing and not mentioning.
variants.medium: One of them has become a person the other does not entirely recognize, and misses the old version out loud.
variants.high: One of them finally says he has been performing a whole life he does not want, and cannot take that back.

variants.low: A goodbye comes out clipped and wrong and neither can fix it in the time left.
variants.medium: One of them leaves without saying it properly, and comes back to a version of the other he did not expect.
variants.high: This is the last chance to say it before something ends for good, and one of them keeps not saying it.

variants.low: There is one place to sleep, and they both make a great show of not caring.
variants.medium: There is one bed, and the careful arrangement of limbs becomes its own conversation.
variants.high: There is one bed, one of them is already asleep against the other, and the awake one has all night to think about it.

variants.low: A photo turns up that one of them has clearly kept for a long time.
variants.medium: A photo turns up that neither can explain casually, and someone else asks about it.
variants.high: The photo makes it obvious how long this has been going on, and both of them are looking at it.

variants.low: It is far too late at night and one of them is being more honest than he means to be.
variants.medium: One of them says the true thing at three in the morning and is not sure the other will remember it.
variants.high: Everything gets said in one exhausted rush, and in the morning neither of them can pretend it did not happen.

variants.low: One of them made a small plan for the weekend that quietly did not include the other.
variants.medium: One of them has been building a future the other is not in, and says so without meaning to.
variants.high: One of them realizes he has been the backup plan in every version of the other's life.

tensions.label: A touch that goes on too long

variants.low: A hand stays somewhere a second longer than a friend's would.
variants.medium: One of them does not let go, and the not-letting-go becomes the whole conversation.
variants.high: Neither of them moves away, and the excuse they have been using for years stops working.

variants.low: A song comes on that one of them clearly has feelings about.
variants.medium: A song comes on that belongs to a night neither of them has ever discussed.
variants.high: One of them admits he taped that song for the other years ago and never handed it over.

tensions.label: The campaign says it for them

variants.low: The campaign takes a turn that is a little too close to home and Mike keeps narrating anyway.
variants.medium: Will's character says the thing Will cannot, and Mike answers in character without thinking.
variants.high: The game stops being a game halfway through the sentence and neither of them picks the dice back up.

variants.low: One of them turned up unannounced and will not fully explain why.
variants.medium: One of them came a long way for this, and says it was for no particular reason.
variants.high: One of them dropped an entire life to be here, and the other works out what that means mid-sentence.

tensions.label: Saying it to somebody else first

variants.low: One of them is trying to work out how to say something to his family and cannot get the words in order.
variants.medium: One of them came out to someone else first, and the other finds out he was not the first to know.
variants.high: One of them is about to say it to a room that may not take it well, and the other has to decide where he is standing.

catalysts.label: The power goes out
catalysts.text: Before either can escape the conversation, the power goes out.

catalysts.label: A song starts
catalysts.text: A song starts playing that neither of them can talk over.

catalysts.label: The door locks
catalysts.text: The door shuts behind them and does not open again.

catalysts.label: The walkie crackles
catalysts.text: The walkie-talkie crackles to life with a voice neither of them expected.

catalysts.label: Someone walks in
catalysts.text: Someone walks in at precisely the wrong moment and immediately understands too much.

catalysts.label: The phone rings
catalysts.text: The phone rings, and whoever is on the other end changes what this night is about.

catalysts.label: It starts raining
catalysts.text: The rain starts, hard, and there is nowhere to go.

catalysts.label: Something old turns up
catalysts.text: One of them turns up something from years ago that neither of them has looked at since.

catalysts.label: The feeling comes back
catalysts.text: That familiar cold goes down one of their necks, and the room changes temperature.

catalysts.label: They run out of time
catalysts.text: Somebody announces they have to go.
